title: Math for ML, Deeper
tagline: The next layer of math behind ML papers: change of basis, SVD, Jacobians, Hessians, convexity, Lagrange multipliers, Gaussians, and KL divergence.
prereqs: Python & Math for AI (vectors, matrices, derivatives, Bayes' theorem, the normal distribution).

steps.title: Span and basis vectors
steps.why: What it means for vectors to build a whole space.

steps.title: Dot products and duality
steps.why: Why a dot product is secretly a projection and a linear map.

steps.title: Change of basis
steps.why: Describe the same vector in different coordinate systems.

steps.title: Singular value decomposition
steps.why: Any matrix factors into rotate or reflect, scale, then rotate or reflect.

steps.title: The multivariable chain rule
steps.why: The rule backpropagation applies over and over.

steps.title: The Jacobian matrix
steps.why: All partial derivatives of a vector function in one matrix.

steps.title: The Hessian matrix
steps.why: Second derivatives describe curvature around a point.

steps.title: Taylor series
steps.why: Approximate a function near a point with polynomials.

steps.title: Convexity
steps.why: Why every local minimum of a convex function is also a global one.

steps.title: Lagrange multipliers
steps.why: Optimize a function while obeying a constraint.

steps.title: The covariance matrix
steps.why: How features vary together, summed up in one matrix.

steps.title: The multivariate Gaussian
steps.why: The bell curve in many dimensions, shaped by covariance.

steps.title: The central limit theorem
steps.why: Why sums of random things look normal.

steps.title: Entropy, cross-entropy, and KL divergence
steps.why: The information theory behind the most common loss function.

projects: Compress a photo with NumPy's SVD at several ranks and plot quality against storage size.
Check your hand-derived Jacobian of a small two-layer network against autograd in PyTorch.
Write a notebook that computes entropy, cross-entropy, and KL divergence for two distributions and shows KL is not symmetric.
